content.intro: Learn Where Is Ruby Used? through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding where is ruby used? helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Where Is Ruby Used? helps you reason about web applications and backend services. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Web applications and backend services. Then connect it to Automation and command-line tools. The remaining syllabus points—Data processing and scripting, Libraries, developer tools, and application infrastructure—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Run, troubleshoot, and reset
content_blocks.text: Save as lesson.rb and run `ruby lesson.rb` from a terminal. CodeLeaf currently has no isolated Ruby runner, so these examples should be run locally until one is deployed.
